_comment: THE BUILD POST. What somebody made, written so another builder would want to look.
spec/analysis.v1.json is about the PERSON: build style, dimensions, archetype,
prompting, growth edge. Four of its seventeen fields describe the work. That is the
right shape for a private profile and the wrong shape for a feed, because nobody has
ever stopped scrolling for somebody else's steering score. This spec is the other
half: what got made, what it does now that it did not before, and what was hard.
scripts/gen_shipped.py emits, all committed, all `git diff --exit-code`'d in CI:
server/builder/shipped_spec.py     Pydantic, extra='forbid', on the way into Postgres
THE HARD PART IS THE POST. `hard_part` is the field this whole spec exists for.
'I built a transit app' is a sentence. 'The map kept dropping overlays because the
native layer applies inserts before removes' is a post, and it is the one thing in
here another builder cannot get anywhere else. It is grounded in measured evidence,
never in a guess: the failure loops, the rewritten files and the runs that produced
nothing are handed to the model as the candidates, and it picks among them.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE: no hours, no token counts, no dollar figures, no
archetype, no scores. Those live on the profile. A build post that leads with how
long it took is a post about the poster.

ShippedChange.name: text
ShippedChange.doc: one thing that is now possible that was not before, in plain words. Not a commit message, not a file name.

ShippedChange.name: evidence
ShippedChange.doc: what in the work shows it: a commit, a test, a number the input gave you. Null when the input only described it.

fields.name: what
fields.doc: one line: what this is. Written for somebody who has never seen the project. Not the repo name, not a commit message, no jargon a non-programmer would miss.

fields.name: why
fields.doc: who it is for and what it lets them do, in one sentence. Null when the work genuinely does not say, which is better than a guess.

fields.name: stage
fields.doc: how far along it is, from what the work shows. Tests and commits say working; a first scaffold says prototype.

fields.name: changes
fields.doc: what is new since last time, each a thing somebody could try. Never a list of files touched.

fields.name: hard_part
fields.doc: the thing that was genuinely difficult, and what it turned out to be. THE FIELD THIS SPEC EXISTS FOR. Grounded in the evidence you were given, never invented. Null when nothing in the work was hard, which is a real answer.

fields.name: stack
fields.doc: technologies actually visible in the work. Never inferred from the kind of project it looks like.

fields.name: demo
fields.doc: the one screenshot or clip that would show this off, named concretely. Null when there is nothing visual to show.

fields.name: next
fields.doc: what is obviously next, only when the work itself says so (a TODO, a failing test left in, a stated intent). Null otherwise.

fields.name: shipped_version
fields.doc: == spec version. A retuned prompt is a recompute, not a migration.

fields.name: model
fields.doc: model id that wrote this, as reported by claude -p

fields.name: dashes_rewritten
fields.doc: dashes rewritten as commas after the fact. Rewritten, never rejected.

fields.name: unsupported_claims_dropped
fields.doc: claims deleted for naming a technology or a fact the work never showed. Above zero means the check is doing work.
